Semantics: a room survives ordinary client and model sessions; an agent session may survive attempt-workspace teardown; an attempt workspace is ephemeral and never canonical authority; bytes existing only in an ephemeral workspace are not durable product state; a candidate becomes durable only through the established exact-candidate path; session reconstruction begins from controller, task and evidence authority and never from unverifiable model memory; a restart must not duplicate the attempt; an unresumable provider session produces an explicit classified result; fresh-session fallback retains task, run and candidate provenance; and a stale session cannot issue new effects.
authorityPrerequisites: model prose is never task state; controller/task/evidence authority is the only reconstruction source
slices.empiricalReview: Negative controls per §1, each observed FAILING the attack: a reconstructed session trusting model prose as task state; a deleted workspace treated as publication evidence; two sessions resuming one exclusive attempt; a stale provider thread executing after a successor exists; an uncommitted sandbox file shown as durable website output.

slices.title: Shared room, multi-participant steering and concurrency
slices.goal: Model participant_id, participant_principal, participant_role, client_kind, room_membership_id, membership_state, joined_at, revoked_at, allowed_read_scope and allowed_intention_scope, with roles at minimum OWNER, OPERATOR, OBSERVER and SYSTEM_AGENT. Product authorization exists only where mechanically enforced and is never inferred from a display label. Every message and intention is attributable to room_id, conversation_id, thread_id, message_id, participant_id, asked_by, client_kind and issued_at. Concurrency: the same command from two clients produces ONE effect via command_id and dedup; expected_watermark guards stale steering; a conversational message cannot mutate a frozen current TaskContract — new scope becomes a new intake source, an amendment proposal or a future task; unauthorized users cannot read private room context; revoked participants lose read and write; Slack display names never impersonate; and web and Slack share one room without two truth stores.
authorityPrerequisites: authorization claims require IDENTITY-01/02 mechanical enforcement; a role label is never a capability
slices.empiricalReview: Negative controls per §2, each observed FAILING: a Slack display name used as authenticated identity; a revoked member still reading; concurrent starts creating two runs; steering silently rewriting a frozen TaskContract; cross-room participant leakage.

slices.title: One versioned Nortropic operator protocol
slices.targetRepository: Nortropic-owned operator protocol plus its clients (Nortropic/verkstadsgolvet, Nortropic Tag and the later adapters)
slices.goal: Define and implement ONE Nortropic-owned versioned operator protocol used by the web, Nortropic Slack, the optional Claude Tag adapter, Channels and Routines, covering snapshot reads, event and backfill reads, task inspection, evidence reference reads, context reads and writes, typed intention proposal, typed intention submission, command status, notifications and standing-work management. Properties: schema_version, request_id, idempotency_key, authenticated_client_id, room_id, expected_watermark where relevant, issued_at, expires_at, pagination/backfill cursor, result status, typed rejection reason and a trace or evidence reference. Behaviour: reconnect loses and duplicates nothing; clients upgrade independently within a documented compatibility window; an unknown major fails closed; unknown future events are inspectable but non-authoritative; rate limiting is explicit; client caches never become truth; no adapter invents a sixth intention; and no client invents an alternative command-status vocabulary. The protocol may be built and tested against a fail-closed fixture implementation before REMOTE-00 exists.
authorityPrerequisites: the five canonical intention verbs and the five command statuses remain closed sets
unknown major version fails closed
slices.empiricalReview: A reconnect is observed losing and duplicating nothing; an unknown major version is observed failing closed; an unknown future event is observed being inspectable and non-authoritative; a client cache is observed never overriding a snapshot; and an adapter attempting a sixth intention or a novel command status is observed being rejected.
slices.dependenciesNote: the contract plus its fixture implementation have no live dependency. Live transport binds REMOTE-00 (backend S13) only.

slices.title: Real remote source intake from Slack
slices.targetRepository: Nortropic Tag (Slack app) plus the intake path
slices.goal: Accept real work from Slack as typed intake SOURCES: plain text, Markdown code blocks, Markdown file attachments, supported Slack file attachments and thread replies referencing a prior source. Preserve per source slack_team_id, slack_channel_id, slack_thread_ts, slack_message_ts, slack_event_id, slack_file_id where present, room_id, participant_id, source_ref, source_sha256 claim, content_type, filename and size_bytes. Slack request and event identity is verified; files are downloaded server-side with the app's scoped credential; type and size limits apply; NO semantic compilation happens in Slack; the controller rereads and rehashes per the canonical intake contract; deleted, expired or inaccessible Slack files produce an explicit rejection; duplicate deliveries produce one source and one command; an edit never silently mutates a stored source (an edit is a new source version or an amendment proposal); and message or file content never reaches generic logs. Before live S10/S13 the complete Slack intake UX and security boundary are still built and tested against fixtures or a fake transport, and no live acceptance is claimed.
authorityPrerequisites: the controller rereads and rehashes the exact bytes; a frontend or Slack-side hash claim is never accepted as authority
slices.empiricalReview: Each source type is observed producing exactly one typed source with all identifiers preserved; a duplicate delivery is observed producing one source; a deleted or inaccessible file is observed producing an explicit rejection; an edited message is observed producing a new version rather than a silent mutation; and no message or file content is observed in generic logs.
remotePrerequisites: a Slack workspace plus the Nortropic-owned Slack app provisioned by the owner (same ceremony as REMOTE-01)
slices.dependenciesNote: REMOTE-01 is the Nortropic Tag slice ('Nortropic Tag — own Slack app'); its fail-closed shell is enough for this slice's non-live half. LIVE acceptance additionally requires backend S10 + S13.

slices.title: Notification delivery, acknowledgement and resolution
slices.goal: Record notification_id, signal_type, severity, room_id, run_id, task_id, dedup_key, created_at, delivery_channel, delivery_status, delivered_at, acknowledged_by, acknowledged_at, snoozed_until, resolved_at, superseded_by and evidence_refs, with statuses at least PENDING, DELIVERED, ACKNOWLEDGED, SNOOZED, RESOLVED, DELIVERY_FAILED and SUPERSEDED. One condition never produces duplicate spam; a resolved condition is never presented as active; an acknowledgement never changes controller truth; payloads carry references, never secrets; model-independent controller alarms work with no model session alive; the conversational Slack client never replaces backend h-014 alarm semantics; and a delivery failure is visible in Verkstadsgolvet. Quiet hours and escalation are explicit policy, never implicit model judgement.
authorityPrerequisites: acknowledgement is never authority: it changes no controller state and satisfies no owner ceremony
h-014 controller-alarm semantics are owned by the backend and are not replaced by any client
slices.empiricalReview: One condition is observed producing one notification across retries; a resolved notification is observed never appearing active; a delivery failure is observed being visible rather than silent; and an acknowledgement is observed changing no controller truth.

slices.title: Narrow standing-work management contract
slices.goal: Separate execution from administration with a SEPARATE versioned management contract — standing_work.create, inspect, update, enable, disable, delete — distinct from the five run/task intentions. Every mutation carries management_command_id, standing_work_id, room_id, authenticated_principal, expected_version, issued_at, expires_at, a typed payload, a status and a rejection reason plus evidence_ref. A stale expected_version is rejected; duplicates produce one effect; disabled standing work never fires; deleted standing work cannot resurrect via stale events; an update never changes historical runs; and standing work only ever creates proposals, sources or ordinary tasks — never candidate, verdict, attestation, promotion or main writes. This contract is FROZEN before any live standing-work write path exists.
authorityPrerequisites: the contract is frozen before live standing-work writes are enabled
the five intention verbs are not extended or overloaded by this contract
slices.empiricalReview: A stale expected_version is observed being rejected; a duplicate management command is observed producing one effect; disabled standing work is observed never firing; a deleted item is observed not resurrecting from a stale event; and an update is observed leaving historical runs unchanged.

slices.goal: Project release_id, preview_deployment_id, production_deployment_id, deployed_commit_sha, production_url, last_known_good_release_id, health_state, smoke_state, incident_id, incident_state, rollback_eligible, rollback_requested_at, rollback_authority, rollback_target_release_id, rollback_completed_at and evidence_refs, with UI states PREVIEW_READY, DEPLOYING, PRODUCTION_HEALTHY, POST_DEPLOY_SMOKE_FAILED, INCIDENT_OPEN, ROLLBACK_ELIGIBLE, ROLLBACK_REQUESTED, ROLLING_BACK, ROLLED_BACK and INCIDENT_RESOLVED. NO automatic rollback is authorized by this requirement alone: a rollback EXECUTION path requires a separately frozen typed contract, authority model, negative controls and exact deployment identity binding. This slice is projection and operator presentation only.
authorityPrerequisites: no rollback execution path is built by this slice; execution requires a separately frozen contract and authority model
production health is read from a real deployment source, never inferred from a Git merge
slices.empiricalReview: Negative controls per §10, each observed FAILING: a preview presented as production; a rollback targeting an unverified release; model prose initiating a rollback; a stale rollback acting after a newer healthy deployment; production health guessed from a Git merge alone.

slices.title: Showroom, context and audit data governance
slices.goal: All showroom data is synthetic and clearly non-customer — no real names, domains, contacts, credentials or proprietary content in generated fixtures — and fixture generation stays schema-derived. Context retention is explicit; deletion is effective; participant revocation is enforced; audit retention is explicit and may differ from conversational-context retention; secrets are redacted before persistence; personal Slack content is stored only per the approved source and context contract; context and audit are exportable in a readable evidence format; cross-customer, cross-room and cross-channel queries fail closed; and production backups respect deletion and retention. Showroom data and production data are never silently joined.
authorityPrerequisites: retention and deletion policy recorded and owner-approved before production data exists
slices.empiricalReview: Generated showroom data is observed containing no real customer artifact; a deletion is observed being effective including in the export path; a cross-room and a cross-customer query are each observed failing closed; and a secret is observed being redacted before persistence.

slices.title: Remote attention is not remote authority
slices.goal: The room and Slack MAY display owner-attention, owner-authority, external-provisioning and legal-human-only conditions and allow acknowledge, open evidence, copy the exact required action, request a fresh inspection and snooze per policy. They may NOT treat a Slack emoji, a button click, an ordinary web session, a model confirmation or a notification acknowledgement as owner authority. Remote owner-action support is a SEPARATE FUTURE AUTHORITY SLICE: until such a protocol has been threat-modelled, test-authored, frozen, mechanically authenticated, replay-protected and candidate/run/task-bound, and independently reviewed, owner-only ceremonies remain FAIL-CLOSED and are clearly explained rather than silently unavailable.
authorityPrerequisites: a separate owner-action protocol threat-modelled, test-authored, frozen, mechanically authenticated, replay-protected, candidate/run/task-bound and independently reviewed BEFORE any remote owner-authority path exists
slices.empiricalReview: An owner-only ceremony is observed being presented as fail-closed with its exact required action; a Slack emoji, a button click, a model confirmation and a notification acknowledgement are each observed NOT satisfying owner authority.
slices.dependenciesNote: no implementation dependencies are listed by design. The display half rides on the room surfaces; the remote owner-ACTION write path is fail-closed until separately threat-modelled and frozen as its own authority slice, and this ledger row must never be read as authorization to build it.

slices.title: Operate Verkstadsgolvet and Nortropic Tag
slices.targetRepository: Nortropic/verkstadsgolvet plus the Nortropic Tag service and their Railway deployment configuration
slices.goal: Record per service: service identity, Railway project/environment/service, deployed commit or version, health endpoint, startup status, dependency status, operator API reachability, last successful event or command, credential rotation date and reference, audit sink status and notification delivery status. The Slack app may be a separately scoped Railway service if architect review shows least privilege; no signing secret or bot token ever reaches the browser; no duplicate Railway project is created without evidence; the health endpoint exposes no secret; logs redact content and credentials; startup with a missing required secret fails closed; a controller outage never makes Slack claim success; a Slack outage never stops the controller; a Verkstadsgolvet outage never changes controller truth; and runbooks cover install, linking, deploy, rotation, revocation and recovery.
authorityPrerequisites: GitHub main auto-deploy remains the single deploy path; railway up must not be used in parallel (erratum-01)
runbook documents are written by a documentation-authority task, not by a product builder
slices.empiricalReview: A CLI-verified deployed SHA and an observed production URL are recorded for each service; a startup with a missing required secret is observed failing closed; the health endpoint is observed exposing no secret; and a simulated controller outage is observed producing no Slack success claim.
